story: Afternoon showers have settled over Sumter Oaks at 4:17 on Tuesday, and Gary has set off toward Town Square in his patient, unhurried way. Donna and Rosa are gathered at Rosa's house, spreading golf cart sketches across the dining table while the rain lasts, with Donna cheerfully insisting she has counted three flamingos twice. Out on Magnolia Loop, Hal is keeping a watchful eye on the flamingo flock and logging the count in his notebook. Rosa remains optimistic that the whole cart plan will be ready to submit to Architectural Review once Hal arrives to pitch in.
events: Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street and log the number in my notebook

gary.thought_process: I've filed the application, checked on it, and left my wiring sketches and clamp list in the drop box. Nobody's here and the committee hasn't answered, so hovering around Town Hall won't speed it up. Rosa and Hal were clear about waiting for the Review sign-off, and I'm not rigging anything until I have it. Halloween parade is Saturday, which is plenty of time if I stay patient. Best use of my afternoon is heading back to the square, where I might run into Rosa, Donna, or Hal and keep my promise to do this the right way, and maybe be useful to somebody in the meantime.

parameters.content: Everything's filed and the sketches are in the drop box. Nothing more to do here but wait on the committee, so I'll go see who's around.

donna.thought_process: Rosa just asked if I got the flamingos down to three. I told her already last tick that I'm at three out front, but she may not have registered it. Hal's on his way, and she wants to sketch the cart before the rain picks up. I shouldn't repeat my question about Architectural Review. Better to confirm briefly, then help move the sketching forward by sitting at the dining table. Keeping everything Review-friendly protects my standing, and this parade planning keeps me at the center of things.

parameters.content: Three flamingos, hon, I counted twice, and Hal logged it in his notebook too. Let's spread those sketches out on the dining table and get the cart drawn up while we wait for him.

hal.thought_process: I'm on Magnolia Loop with nobody in sight, and the flamingo flock is the very thing I came to keep honest. My notebook count can't be trusted if I rely on yesterday's tally, and Donna pulled six off the lawn. I should look at the flock myself and log the number accurately before I decide whether there's anything to report to the committee. If she's at three, I'll admit it and let it go; fair is fair, and a rule is a rule for everybody.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street and log the number in my notebook

rosa.thought_process: Donna just asked about Architectural Review on the parade cart sketches. I haven't submitted anything yet, since Gary and I agreed to keep everything removable until approval and we haven't finished the sketches. Hal is still on his way. Honest answer: no word yet because nothing's been filed, and we should sketch first, then submit. I shouldn't repeat my earlier ask about the ornaments since she already answered it (down to three). Move things forward by answering her and proposing we start sketching at the dining table while the rain keeps us inside.

parameters.content: Nothing to hear yet, hon, we haven't filed anything. Let's get the sketches done at the dining table while this rain lasts, and Hal can pitch in when he gets here. Then I'll submit the whole thing to Architectural Review.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
